findings.subject: search
findings.message: The strategy "lift and shift" of the application "search" is not one of the seven (retire, retain, rehost, relocate, repurchase, replatform, refactor), so the cutover and wave checks were skipped for it.
findings.fix: Use one of the seven names.

basis.text: There are seven migration strategies for moving applications to the cloud, known as the 7 Rs:
A migration strategy is the approach used to migrate a workload into the AWS Cloud.

findings.subject: notifications
findings.message: The application "notifications" depends on "email-relay", which is not an id in this plan, so nothing says where or when that dependency moves.
findings.fix: Add "email-relay" to the plan (with the strategy retain if it does not move), or correct the id.

basis.text: Map internal and external dependencies to discover these connections before creating migration groups.
basis.section: Group dependent systems within the same wave

findings.subject: catalog
findings.message: The applications "catalog" and "inventory-sync" depend on each other in a loop, so no order of waves can put each one after what it needs.
findings.fix: Check the links and remove the one that is not real. If the applications truly need each other, plan them as one unit: one entry of the plan, in one wave.

basis.text: Move all directly connected components together to maintain performance and avoid disruptions.
basis.section: Group dependent systems within the same wave, direct dependencies

findings.subject: orders-api
findings.message: The application "orders-api" moves in wave 1 and depends on "orders-db", which moves later, in wave 2. Between the two waves "orders-api" runs in the new environment and calls back to the old one, or does not work at all.
findings.fix: Move "orders-db" in wave 1 or earlier, or move "orders-api" in wave 2 with it.

basis.text: Dependencies between workloads cause service disruptions if not migrated together.
basis.section: Group dependent systems within the same wave

basis.text: You must identify workloads that communicate or share resources and group them into the same migration wave.
basis.section: Group dependent systems within the same wave

findings.subject: reports
findings.message: The application "reports" (rehost, wave 3) depends on "legacy-ledger", which is planned for retire. When "legacy-ledger" is shut down, "reports" loses something it needs.
findings.fix: Remove the dependency first (replace or move what "reports" uses), or do not retire "legacy-ledger" while something depends on it.

basis.text: Retiring the application means that you can shut down the servers within that application stack.
Dependencies between workloads cause service disruptions if not migrated together.
basis.section: Group dependent systems within the same wave

findings.subject: pricing
findings.message: The application "pricing" (refactor, wave 1) has no rollback plan, so if the cutover fails nothing written says how to go back or when to decide it.
findings.fix: Write the rollback steps, and the condition that starts them, in the rollback field.

basis.text: Always establish rollback criteria and procedures before initiating any migration or deployment.
A rollback plan enables teams to quickly reverse changes when a deployment fails or introduces risk.

findings.subject: orders-db
findings.message: The application "orders-db" (replatform, wave 2) is stateful and names no data sync method, so nothing says how its data reaches the new environment and stays current until the cutover.
findings.fix: Name the method in data_sync (for example replication or backup-restore), and say how writes are paused at the cutover.

basis.text: Near-zero downtime migration ensures that critical workloads remain operational during the transition through continuous data replication and cutover techniques.
basis.section: Choose the migration method for each workload

basis.text: Downtime migration is simpler and faster because it doesn't require real-time synchronization between source and target environments.
basis.section: Choose the migration method for each workload

findings.subject: inventory-sync
findings.message: The application "inventory-sync" has no strategy, so the tool cannot tell whether it moves, stays or is retired, and the cutover and wave checks were skipped for it.
findings.fix: Choose one of the seven strategies for the application: retire, retain, rehost, relocate, repurchase, replatform or refactor.

basis.text: A migration strategy is the approach used to migrate a workload into the AWS Cloud.

findings.subject: pricing
findings.message: The application "pricing" has no owner, so nobody is named to approve its cutover, its rollback or its retirement.
findings.fix: Name the team or the person who owns the application.

basis.text: Use the migration adoption plan to verify details like business unit, workload owner, technical dependencies, and criticality classification.

findings.subject: reports
findings.message: The application "reports" (rehost, wave 3) has no test plan, so nothing says how the team will know that the application works after the move.
findings.fix: Write the tests that prove the application works after the cutover, for example end-to-end tests of its main business flows, in the test_plan field.

basis.text: Run end-to-end tests to confirm that the application functions correctly with the migrated data.

findings.subject: orders-web
findings.message: The DNS TTL of the application "orders-web" is 3,600 seconds and its cutover window is 30 minutes (1,800 seconds). A resolver may keep the old address for as long as the TTL, so clients can still reach the old environment after the window has closed.
findings.fix: Lower the TTL to the length of the window or less, and do it at least one old TTL before the cutover starts.

basis.text: a 32 bit signed integer that specifies the time interval that the resource record may be cached before the source of the information should again be consulted.
Update DNS records and load balancer configurations to direct user traffic to the Azure environment.

findings.subject: wave 2
findings.message: Wave 2 holds 4 applications, and the limit given with --max-apps-per-wave is 3. A wave that is bigger than the team planned for leaves less room to test, to fix and to roll back.
findings.fix: Move 1 application to another wave (keeping dependencies in order), or raise the limit if the team can carry it.

basis.text: Migration wave planning divides large migration projects into smaller, manageable groups of workloads that can be migrated together.
Set wave durations based on workload complexity and team capacity.

findings.subject: pricing
findings.message: The application "pricing" moves (refactor, wave 1) and depends on "mainframe-billing", which is retained in the source environment. After the move this link crosses from the new environment to the old one. This is not an error; it is a link to plan for.
findings.fix: Plan the link across both environments (network path, latency, firewall rules and who owns it), and write down when "mainframe-billing" will move, if ever.

basis.text: This is the migration strategy for applications that you want to keep in your source environment or applications that you are not ready to migrate.
Create a clear plan with timelines and risk management approaches to reduce the time your workload operates across both environments.
